text: . External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar, will be on a five day visit to Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire and Ethiopia from today. During the visit, Dr Jaishankar will hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts and meet with leadership of all three nations to review close bilateral ties of friendship and cooperation. Discussions will cover whole gamut of bilateral ties across sectors, including trade and economic, development cooperation, capacity building, and people to people ties. He will also exchange perspectives on regional and global matters of mutual interest. In Addis Ababa, External Affairs Minister will also chair the Regional Heads of Mission (HoMs) Conference. Ministry of External Affairs said, the visit of Dr Jaishankar is reflective of India’s commitment to deepen its partnership with Africa, and will further India’s solidarity with Global South.

. The seven OPEC-plus countries – Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman, have decided to maintain their September 2026 production quotas unchanged for November.The decision was taken during a virtual meeting on October 4, where the countries reviewed global oil market conditions and outlook.  The group will continue to meet monthly, with the next meeting scheduled for November 1.Separately, the 68th meeting of the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) stressed the importance of protecting international maritime routes and energy infrastructure, warning that attacks or disruptions could increase market volatility and affect energy supply.

. The National Statistics Office (NSO) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation has conducted the first-ever all-India survey on household travel. The survey covered 14 thousand 274 villages and 10,377 urban blocks and collected information from around four lakh 92 thousand  households, covering over  20 lakh 34 thousand persons.According to National Household Travel Survey which was conducted during July, 2025 to  June this year, two-wheelers are the predominant mode of transport for commuting to fixed workplaces, accounting for 42.6 per cent of workers. The average monthly expenditure on commuting to a fixed workplace is 785 rupees per worker, while the  Urban workers incur a substantially higher average monthly cost of one thousand and 44 rupees, compared with 612 rupees for rural workers.It added that buses and railways facilitate 73.5 percent of  overnight travel followed by cars at 15.1 percent and two wheelers at 8.8 percent. The Ministry said that the primary objective of the survey is to generate robust, data-driven insights into domestic travel patterns and dynamics to support regional transport planning, infrastructure development and evidence-based policy formulation.

. The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave will be held from this Saturday in New Delhi, under the theme of ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’. The Ministry of Finance said that the three-day gathering will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries.The Ministry added that the Conclave will feature plenary sessions, interactive parallel sessions and roundtables. The roundtables will focus on issues including attracting foreign direct investment and mobilising domestic capital for long-term investment. The Ministry said that these roundtables will provide opportunities for more focused exchanges among policymakers, economists, investors and practitioners.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will deliver the inaugural address on the first day of the conclave. The conclave will also witness addresses from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and other Union Ministers. The Ministry informed that the conclave will also feature a special address by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Sanjay Malhotra.

. Himachal’s four women kabaddi players, including Pushpa Rana- captain of the Indian women’s kabaddi team that won the gold medal at Asian Games, today met Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. During the meeting, the players requested that the government increase the prize money from rupees 33 lakhs to Rs. one crore and sought employment at the rank of DSP.Following the meeting, Rana stated that their primary demand was to raise the prize money to Rs. 1 crore. She mentioned that the Chief Minister responded positively to their requests and assured them that they would be fulfilled.On this occasion, Pushpa Rana also urged the youth to stay away from drugs and embrace sports. She remarked that sports not only pave the way for a better future but also inspire young people to lead healthy and disciplined lives.It is noteworthy that Himachal’s daughters, Pushpa Rana, Ritu Negi, Jyoti Thakur, and Bhavna Thakur, played a pivotal role in India’s golden victory at the Asian Games. The players expressed that the state government’s support would motivate them to deliver even better performances in the future.

. In China Open Tennis, Serbian Novak Djokovic has stormed into the men’s singles final after Daniil Medvedev of Russia was defaulted during their semi-final clash in Beijing. The record six-time champion was serving for the match at 7-5, 5-3, 15/15 when a ball rebounded off the back wall. Medvedev instinctively struck the ball, sending it into the crowd where it hit a spectator, resulting in his default. Djokovic has now reached his first ATP 500 final since winning the title in Astana in 2022. He will face fifth-seeded Australian Alex de Minaur today.

. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met US business leaders and discussed opportunities to further deepen partnerships and investments in India. Mr Goyal met Jonathan Gray, President & COO of Blackstone, George Walker, Chairman and CEO of Nueberger Berman, and Stephane de La Faverie, President & CEO of The Estee Lauder Companies in New York yesterday. Mr Goyal also held a productive meeting with George Walker, Chairman & CEO of Neuberger Berman, along with Anthony Tutrone, Global Head of Neuberger Markets; Andrew Komaroff, COO; and Zain Naqi, Managing Director. He said with resilient macroeconomic fundamentals and deepening capital markets, India offers unmatched scale and long-term value creation for global institutional investors. Mr Goyal also held a meeting with Stephane de La Faverie, President & CEO of The Estee Lauder Companies in New York. Mr Goyal was in the US to participate in the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting. He also met US business leaders in Chicago and addressed the Indian diaspora.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey asserted that India needs capital markets that can mobilise capital, manage risk and build investor confidence.While addressing the 12th International Convention of the Commodity and Capital Market Participants Association of India in New Delhi today, he said, the regulator is working to strengthen the market structure so that households can invest with confidence, businesses can raise funds for growth, and market intermediaries maintain high standards of conduct. SEBI Chairman said, the regulator is examining concerns related to the settlement price framework for derivatives on expiry days following the introduction of the Closing Auction Session – CAS. The mechanism was introduced to improve price discovery for eligible stocks at market close by using a call-auction process to determine a single equilibrium price instead of relying solely on volume-weighted average prices.He also said, SEBI is working to deepen and improve liquidity in cash markets, expand participation and strengthen securities borrowing and lending. He added that efficient hedging and arbitrage can improve price discovery and strengthen the interaction between cash and derivatives markets. The regulator is also examining position limits for non-agricultural contracts with the aim of improving market liquidity and depth while maintaining risk controls.

. President Droupadi Murmu will be on a three-day visit to Himachal Pradesh beginning today. The President will attend the first convocation ceremony of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Bilaspur, as the Chief Guest today. Following the convocation ceremony, the President is scheduled to travel to ManaliOn the first day of her three-day visit to Himachal Pradesh, President Droupadi Murmu will attend the first convocation ceremony of AIIMS, Bilaspur, as the Chief Guest and confer degrees upon the graduating doctors. According to the proposed programme, the President will reach AIIMS at around 10:30 this morning. Governor of Himachal Pradesh Kavinder Gupta, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, and Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda will also attend the convocation ceremony.On the second day of her Himachal Pradesh visit, October 7, President Murmu will visit the famous Hidimba Temple in Manali and also the Atal Tunnel in Rohtang.Meanwhile, elaborate security arrangements have been made in Bilaspur and Kullu districts in view of the President’s visit. Additional police personnel and security forces have been deployed at the AIIMS premises as well as along the routes to be taken by the President. The President is scheduled to return to Delhi on the morning of October 8.

. The National Statistics Office (NSO), is conducting the Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2026) during the period of October to December 2026.The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said that the survey is aimed at generating comprehensive and timely information on capital expenditure undertaken and planned by large private corporate sector enterprises. The Ministry added that the survey will provide important inputs for understanding emerging investment trends in the Indian economy.The primary objective of the CAPEX Survey is to collect information on capital expenditure undertaken in the recent financial years , provisional capital expenditure in the current financial year and investment intentions for the forthcoming financial year.The Ministry has appealed all the selected private corporate sector enterprises to extend their full cooperation and participate actively in the CAPEX 2026 Survey.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. India’s women’s cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down as captain across all three formats. The 37-year-old announced her decision after a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati. Harmanpreet led India to its maiden ODI World Cup title last year and also guided the team to gold at the Asian Games. She captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, having led the T20 side since 2016 and taken charge of the ODI team in 2022. Harmanpreet will continue to represent India as a player across formats.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. The death toll after a Nigerian military plane flying from Benin City to Lagos crashed has climbed to 32. The 32 victims comprised 25 passengers and seven crew members. President Bola Tinubu confirmed that there were no survivors and directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately launch a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash. According to Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo, the Air Force ATR-42 aircraft was on a routine mission yesterday when air traffic controllers lost contact with it. The wreckage was later located near the coastal town of Igbokoda in southwestern Nigeria, close to a naval base, and search and rescue teams were deployed.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today said the Global South expects India to articulate the region’s concerns in front of the global stage. Addressing the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi on the theme “India and the World: Adaptive by Design”, Dr Jaishankar stated that India voices concerns of the Global South countries, including concerns relating to the four Fs – food, fuel, fertiliser and finance.The External Affairs Minister remarked that India’s approach of multialignment enables it to engage with all important players in the world, including US, Russia and China. He termed US as one of India’s principal strategic partners, largest economic and trade account and major critical defence partner. He maintained that in this age of flux, India should confidently push ahead on every front. He opined that the world is moving towards multipolarity whose architecture and geometry are very different from the way it used to be.

. United States, Canada and eight Latin American and Caribbean countries have accused Iran and its proxies of terrorist activities and other malign operations in the Western Hemisphere and pledged greater coordination to counter them. The joint declaration followed a US-Paraguay forum held last month to strengthen law enforcement cooperation against what Washington describes as Iranian terrorist activity in the region. The governments accused Iran and its proxies of engaging in lethal plotting, illicit fundraising, political interference and foreign influence operations across the hemisphere. The joint statement said, they stand united in determination to protect the countries and people against such threats. The statement was signed by the governments of the United States, Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru and Trinidad and Tobago.

. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres has warned member states about the consequences of failing to reform the UN Security Council. According to Deputy Spokesperson Farhan Haq, Guterres also encouraged the member nations to move forward with the stalled reform process. Haq made the remarks when asked about comments by External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar that the UN’s highest decision-making body must be reformed to remain relevant, given that UN membership has nearly quadrupled since the organisation was established in 1945. Haq said Guterres has consistently maintained that, as the United Nations has expanded, the Security Council must also expand and become more representative of the wider membership.

. The Asian Games 2026 have officially concluded at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya, bringing more than two weeks of action-packed competition across 43 disciplines to an end. The President of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) officially declared the Games closed, marking the conclusion of a memorable edition of the continental sporting event. The ceremonial torch and flag from the inaugural Asian Games were handed over to representatives of Qatar, which will host the next edition in Doha in 2030. The handover marks the official transition from Nagoya 2026 to Doha 2030. Indian shooter Neeru Dhanda, who won two gold medals and a silver during the Games, carried the Indian flag as the country’s flag-bearer at the closing ceremony. India finished fourth in the overall medal standings, with an impressive 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver, and 37 bronze.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended compliments to every member of the Indian contingent as the Asian Games 2026 draw to a close, for representing the nation with determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit. In his message, he congratulated all the medal winners whose performances have brought immense joy to the nation. He hoped that these games would inspire even greater achievements in the years ahead and strengthen sports at the grassroots too.

. Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) flows turned negative in September after positive flows in July and August. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have offloaded Indian equities worth 35,861 crore rupees last month. Out of the total net outflows, 45,537 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges, as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated US bond yields, and crude oil prices weighed on investors’ risk appetite. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market continued last month, with FPIs infusing 9,676 crore rupees in the primary market in September.Meanwhile, foreign investors also extended their selling to the debt market during the period under review. Last month, outflows from the debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 10,431 crore rupees. FPIs withdrew 5,247 crore rupees through General Limit route and 5,049 crore rupees through Voluntary Retention Route (VRR).

. In Men’s Cricket, India will face West Indies in the first match of the five-match T20 International series at the Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium in Lucknow today. The match will start at 7 PM IST. After winning gold at the 2026 Asian Games and a convincing 2-1 win in the One Day International series, the hosts will aim to continue their winning run against the West Indies. As many as 10 members of India’s Asian Games 2026 team have been picked for the series, while three players from the ODI squad are also part of the team. West Indies, on the other hand, have brought in a few power-packed reinforcements for the T20 International in the form of Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell and Romario Shepherd. The next four T20 matches will be played in Ranchi, Indore, Hyderabad and Bengaluru on 9, 11, 14 and 17, of this month.

. India’s National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore teleconsultations, marking a significant milestone in the Government’s efforts to leverage digital technology to make quality healthcare more accessible, affordable and equitable for citizens across the country. The platform recorded over 50 lakhs teleconsultations cumulatively across all States and Union Territories. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said that the achievement reflects the growing role of telemedicine in complementing the country’s existing healthcare delivery system and in overcoming barriers of distance, geography and access, particularly for citizens living in rural, remote and underserved areas.eSanjeevani has emerged as an important component of the country’s digital health ecosystem and as the world’s largest telemedicine implementation in primary healthcare. Further, the platform has extended the reach of public healthcare services beyond the physical boundaries of conventional health facilities and brought medical consultations closer to people in the communities where they live.The service has witnessed rapid and sustained expansion since its inception. The initiative currently supports more than 1.42 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir spokes, over 19 thousand medical hubs and 901 online OPDs, with over two lakh registered healthcare providers. The platform is facilitating around 2.5 to 3 lakh consultations every day in 15 languages, including English and 14 Indian languages. Its highest single-day utilisation has crossed six lakh consultations.Women account for over 57 per cent of total utilisation, while 40 per cent of consultations are availed by citizens aged 46 years and above, including 16.25 per cent by senior citizens aged 60 years and above.The platform has evolved with the integration of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Clinical Decision Support System (AI-CDSS), which supports healthcare providers during consultations and assists in strengthening the quality, consistency and efficiency of clinical decision-making. The innovation has received national recognition with the Gold Award under the National Awards for e-Governance 2026. eSanjeevani has also been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System-112, enabling stronger linkages between emergency response services and remote medical expertise. The integration is aimed at facilitating more coordinated access to medical support and further strengthening the use of digital technology in emergency healthcare.eSanjeevani is now expanding to facilitate specialist OPD consultations through premier government medical institutions. Patient-to-doctor teleconsultation services for select specialities have been rolled out at AIIMS Jodhpur, AIIMS Jammu and AIIMS Patna.eSanjeevani is a Made-in-India digital health solution developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), with C-DAC Mohali providing end-to-end technological development and engineering support since its inception. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has played a central role in guiding the continuous evolution of the platform in response to the emerging needs of India’s healthcare system.

. India and Switzerland today inked five agreements following bilateral talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin in New Delhi.These agreements are on Migration and Mobility Partnership, Exchange of Young Professionals, Promotion and Collaboration on Transportation Technologies, Mobility Systems and Infrastructure in Identified Areas, Letter of Intent between Department of Science and Technology and Swiss National Science Foundation and Implementation Arrangement for cooperation in Innovation, Technology Transfer and Entrepreneurship.In a joint press meet, Prime Minister Modi appreciated Swiss President Guy Parmelin’s commitment to India-Switzerland relations. He said that India implemented the historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement with the European Free Trade Association, EFTA, countries last October.Mr Modi noted that the agreement was India’s first Free Trade Agreement with a European economic bloc. He described it as an ambitious framework for investment, innovation, employment and shared prosperity. The Prime Minister highlighted that under the agreement, India aims to attract 100 billion US dollars in investment and create ten lakh direct jobs over the next 15 years.Prime Minister Modi said that India and Switzerland have taken several important decisions to enhance market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries. He said, this will increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles and engineering goods to Switzerland.Mr Modi said that at the same time, India will attract new Swiss investments in important sectors, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing and sustainability. Prime Minister said, through these initiatives, the two nations will work together to develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the entire world. He said, both the nations today  identified new possibilities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. Mr Modi said the they have also agreed to further deepen cooperation in nuclear energy.The Prime Minister said, the friendship between India and Switzerland goes back centuries. He said, in the 19th century, Swami Vivekananda saw a glimpse of the Himalayas in the Swiss Alps. Mahatma Gandhi also spent time in Switzerland and interacted with its people. Mr Modi said, the memories of these historic visits continue to resonate in the friendship even today.President Parmelin arrived in New Delhi this morning on a three-day state visit to India, accompanied by a high-level delegation comprising senior officials and business leaders. He was received by Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Ajay Tamta at the airport. The visiting dignitary was accorded a ceremonial welcome at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the Swiss President. He was given a tri-services guard of honour.Talking to reporters after the ceremonial welcome, Mr Parmelin said that the visit is an excellent opportunity to emphasise the importance that both Switzerland and India attach to this relationship. He said, the relationship between the two countries is built on shared democratic values, as well as on trust and mutual respect. Swiss President said that his visit is a stepping stone towards further growth, deepening and strengthening of our close, broad and long-standing partnership.External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar also called on President Parmelin. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar appreciated President Parmelin’s sentiments towards deepening the India-Switzerland partnership, building on the promise of India – EFTA TEPA.  He expressed confidence that Mr Parmelin’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi will further engagement across a wide range of domains.The visiting dignitary paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat.President Parmelin will meet President Droupadi Murmu this evening. President Murmu will also host an official banquet in the honour of her Swiss Counterpart.

. The Indian boxing contingent has returned to New Delhi following a triumphant campaign at the 2026 Asian Games. Speaking to the media upon her arrival, boxer Lovlina Borgohain who clinched gold in the Women’s 75 kg category on her birthday shared that the timing made the milestone particularly special. She noted that competing in her second Asian Games gave her the opportunity to upgrade her previous silver medal to gold.While, Boxer Ankush Panghal who also won gold in Men’s 80 kilogram event also expressed his happiness for winning the medal. He said that now he is focusing on the Olympics.Indian boxer Parveen Hooda, who clinched a historic gold medal in the women’s 65 kilogram category has attributed the team’s triumphant campaign to collective hard work and strong institutional backing.   Expressing gratitude, She credited the athletes’ tireless dedication, the strategic guidance of the coaching staff, and the continuous support provided by the Sports Authority of India.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India’s economic strength and resilience have been built over the past decade through a combination of fiscal prudence, infrastructure investment, banking reforms, improved delivery mechanisms and consistent reforms.Addressing the 5th Kautilya economic conclave in New Delhi, the Finance Minister said that the government has advanced the national frameworks through GST, insolvency and bankruptcy code and the four labour codes. She said that India had navigated the shocks of the past four years with its fundamentals intact, citing 7.8 percent real GDP growth in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27.The Finance Minister said that the IMF projects India’s general government debt to decline from 83.4 percent of GDP in 2026 to 77.7 percent in 2031 against a rising global trend.On infrastructure development, Ms Sitharaman said, capital expenditure for this fiscal had been budgeted at 12.22 lakh crore rupees. She added that the national highway network had expanded by about 61 per cent and the number of operational airports had more than doubled since 2014.She also highlighted that more than 52 crore collateral-free loans have been sanctioned under PM MUDRA Yojana. Highlighting the PM Awas Yojana, PM Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, Ms Sitaharaman said that these initiatives have strengthened citizens’ capacity to participate in growth and build capacities to fight the challenges.

. US President Donald Trump has said that he personally believes Iran was responsible for the terrorist attack carried out by an Omani co-pilot aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Trump said this while responding to media queries on the White House premises. The remarks came following the foiled mid-air hijacking and crash attempt aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on 30th of last month, when Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit. The attack was thwarted after Captain Machchhar, despite being severely injured, succeeded in opening the cockpit door. The incident has drawn attention to the actions of Machchhar, who was praised by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a hero of Israel, India, and the world.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. India has voiced support for Afghanistan’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, reaffirming its commitment to the welfare of the Afghan people at the 8th Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan, hosted by Russia in Moscow. Indian delegation was led by Ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar and Joint Secretary (PAI) Dr. M. Suresh Kumar. The consultations were attended by representatives from Russia, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, with Afghanistan represented by Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi. Belarus and Egypt participated as guests.According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, participants reaffirmed the need to develop cooperation with Kabul on an equal and mutually beneficial basis and support Afghanistan’s integration into the global economy. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the forum brings together countries seeking equal and mutually beneficial partnerships with Afghanistan. The Moscow Format was established in 2017 to promote national reconciliation and peace in Afghanistan. On the sidelines of the meeting, Lavrov held talks with Foreign Minister Muttaqi on bilateral cooperation and coordination in international and regional forums.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.

. Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, Shaktikanta Das has said that restoration of the health of the financial sector has been the defining feature of India’s resilience in recent years. He said, India’s financial sector has emerged as a strong pillar of economic growth, supported by reforms such as the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, bank recapitalization and constructive regulatory oversight. He was speaking at the Kautilya Economic Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today. Mr Das highlighted that the Gross non-performing assets have fallen sharply to 1.68 percent in June this year, while bank profitability has improved significantly. Mr Das said the prudent management of the external sector has also supported India’s efforts towards macroeconomic stability. He also mentioned that India’s external sector indicators have remained broadly resilient due to a mix of factors like the ongoing diversification of exports, conclusion of free trade agreements and sustained surplus in services trade. Mr Das said that the current account deficit for 2025-26 remained well within manageable levels at 0.6 percent of GDP.Secretary in the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Saurabh Garg, today said India’s economic resilience, supported by strong corporate performance and sustained investment activity, is now being reflected in upward revisions to the country’s growth estimates by various international agencies. Talking to the media on the sidelines of the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, Mr. Garg said, the Indian economy had maintained its momentum after recording 7.8 per cent growth in the first quarter of the financial year 2026-27. He noted that strong corporate performance and continued capital investment, including by the private sector, were among the key indicators of the positive economic trend. He added that this momentum was also reflected in recent upward revisions to India’s growth projections by international ratings agencies and research firms, including S&P Global Ratings and Fitch Ratings.On the impact of tensions in West Asia and risks arising from global oil price shocks, Mr. Garg highlighted that government interventions, along with measures taken by households and the private sector, had helped limit the adverse impact of external shocks on the Indian economy.

. Vice President C P. Radhakrishnan has said that Sanskrit is the golden string which connects all the Indian languages. Addressing the Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University in New Delhi today, Mr Radhakrishnan said, every Indian language is great and they have contributed towards the culture of the nation. He said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has taken several initiatives for the promotion of the Sanskrit language along with other languages.The Vice President said, the National Education Policy 2020 has further strengthened this vision by placing special emphasis on the Indian Knowledge System. He said, it encourages universities and educational institutions to incorporate the Indian Knowledge System into their academic programmes. Mr Radhakrishnan said, Sanskrit holds a glorious place in the world of science, literature, and philosophy. He said, even today, rare Sanskrit manuscripts are found not only in India but also in countries such as Nepal, Tibet and China. The Vice President said, the launch of the Gyan Bharatam Mission by the Government marks another significant step.In his address, Union Minister of State for Education Dr Sukanta Majumdar said, India is moving forward by combining its rich traditions with modern technology. He said the National Education Policy 2020 has placed Indian languages and traditions at the centre of education so that students remain connected with their roots. Mr. Majumdar urged students to understand Sanskrit along with emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and digital technology, in the era of rapid technological advancement.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices were trading over half a per cent up in the forenoon session today. The Sensex rose 462 points to 72,845, while the Nifty added 140 points to 22,696, when reports last came in. On the sectoral front, Power, Capital Goods and Oil and Gas emerged as the top gainers, while Hospitals, IT, and Realty led the decline.

. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 are set to conclude today, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end. India has put up an impressive performance at the 20th Asian Games, securing fourth place in the overall medal standings with a tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.The closing ceremony of the games will be held at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya, Japan. The event is scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM IST. India’s women’s flag-bearer for the closing ceremony has been confirmed as shooting star Neeru Dhanda, who will proudly carry the Tricolour in Nagoya. The ceremony will feature traditional closing proceedings, including the parade of athletes and the formal handover to the Doha 2030 organising committee.

. The Indian Embassy in Bucharest has informed that all three Indian nationals aboard the commercial vessel MV ROYAD MAMMADOV are safe. The vessel came under attack in the Black Sea, leading to the reported deaths of two foreign nationals. In a series of posts, the Embassy said that it has spoken to the Indian nationals. It further said that one of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. The Embassy said it is extending all possible support for the welfare and well-being of the Indian crew members and is in close touch with the hospital authorities.Furthermore, Indian Ambassador to Romania Manoj Mohapatra spoke to three Indian nationals receiving treatment at Constanța County Hospital. The Ambassador assured them of all possible assistance and support.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined by 18.3 billion US dollars (USD) to 747.5 billion US dollars during the week ended the 25th of September. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 15.5 billion USD to 615.4 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 2.5 billion USD to 108.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 97 million USD to 18.64 billion USD. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped by 86 million to 4.8 billion USD.

Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu today said that the West Asia crisis is one of the major concerns, as it has put a significant burden leading to rise in aviation turbine fuel ATF prices. Talking to media in New Delhi, Mr. Naidu said that the government is in discussions with airlines and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) regarding ATF prices to assess the situation. He said that the ministry will hold a meeting with all stakeholders and then take a decision.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said India needs a strong and integrated maritime ecosystem to further enhance its maritime power and strengthen the country’s defence capabilities.The Defence Minister today launched Fleet Support Ship-1, laid the keel for Fleet Support Ship-5 and inaugurated the upgraded Slipway-4 and a 300-tonne Goliath Crane at Hindustan Shipyard Limited in Visakhapatnam.Addressing the gathering, Mr Singh said the launch of Fleet Support Ship-1, keel laying of Fleet Support Ship-5 and inauguration of upgraded infrastructure at HSL mark important steps in strengthening India’s maritime capabilities.He said Fleet Support Ship-1, named ‘Surya’, will strengthen the Indian Navy’s reach, endurance and operational effectiveness. He said the new slipway and Goliath crane at HSL will further enhance the shipyard’s capacity to undertake large shipbuilding projects.The Defence Minister said the Indian Navy has repeatedly demonstrated its capabilities in the Indian Ocean Region as a first responder and preferred security partner. He said the Navy has played an important role in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, anti-piracy operations, evacuation missions and maritime security.Mr Singh said, Hindustan Shipyard Limited has played an important role in meeting India’s maritime and defence requirements for more than eight decades. He said the shipyard’s Miniratna Category-I status, accorded in 2025, reflects its transformation and improved financial position.The Defence Minister said the Navy, shipyards, DRDO, academia, industry, MSMEs and start-ups need to work together as an integrated team to build a strong national maritime ecosystem.Mr Singh said India has immense potential in shipbuilding, but the challenge is to convert this potential into capability and global competitiveness. He stressed the need to focus on timely delivery, productivity, indigenous design capability, resilient supply chains, skilled manpower, capacity expansion and cost competitiveness.He said India’s defence manufacturing sector has undergone significant transformation over the past decade, with the country moving from dependence on imported platforms towards designing and manufacturing advanced systems and platforms domestically.Mr Singh said India aims to become a developed nation by 2047, with a self-reliant, secure and prosperous economy and a respected position in the world.

. India concluded its campaign at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings. India’s 2026 Asian Games campaign produced a series of landmark achievements across disciplines.The defining feature of India’s campaign was its clean sweep of gold medals in men’s and women’s cricket, kabaddi and hockey. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games concluded yesterday, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end.In cricket, India retained both titles. The women’s team defeated Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final, while the men’s team overcame Pakistan by 19 runs to complete the golden double.Kabaddi also produced a clean sweep. The women’s team defeated Iran 37-34 to successfully defend its title, while the men came from behind to beat Iran 40-34.Hockey also completed the sweep. The Indian women ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games medal by defeating China 1-0, with Lalremsiami scoring the decisive goal in the 10th minute. It was India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games since 1982.The men’s team defeated Malaysia 5-1 to retain its title and claim India’s fifth men’s hockey gold, following triumphs in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022.It was also the first time India’s men’s and women’s hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games. Both teams secured qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.Archery was one of India’s most successful disciplines, producing nine medals – five gold, two silver and two bronze. Boxing produced India’s best Asian Games campaign in terms of gold medals, with three gold and three bronze medals.Indian wrestlers won six medals – two gold, two silver and two bronze, making it the country’s best Asian Games wrestling tally since Jakarta 1962.

. BJP has announced the name of eight candidates for upcoming Rajya Sabha polls for Uttar Pradesh. Party has fielded Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan, and Shruti Gangwar. The names were approved by the BJP Central Election Committee. Today is the last day for filing nominations for the biennial elections.Polling for the Rajya Sabha seats across Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal will be held on 16th of this month. The elections will cover 10 seats from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, along with a bypoll to one seat from West Bengal.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. Renowned British novelist Jeffrey Archer has passed away. He was 86. The news of the demise of Jeffrey Archer, also a former politician, was confirmed by his publisher via a statement. As per them, Archer died suddenly and peacefully at home yesterday. A cause of death was not disclosed. Archer, a former Conservative member of British Parliament, sold more than 300 million books during a writing career that spanned five decades.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government has launched a major military offensive against the Houthi movement, with government forces claiming advances around the key strategic posts along the Red Sea coast. The offensive, formally named “Operation Dawn of Yemen” by President of the Presidential Leadership Council Rashad Al Alimi, today aims to retake territory held by the Houthis, restore state institutions and regain control of the capital, Sanaa, which the group has controlled since 2014. Al Alimi had announced the start of the military campaign a day earlier, saying it was aimed at reclaiming the remaining Houthi-held territory and extending state authority across Yemen.Yemen’s armed forces said they carried out 1,122 precision operations against Houthi targets across Saada, Al Jawf, Taiz and the western coast. Military spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah Al Nuzaili said the operations targeted artillery and rocket-launcher positions, defensive fortifications, supply routes, reinforcements and command-and-control centres.Government forces also reportedly claimed to have taken control of positions around Bab Al Mandab and the Dhubab area. Another news report, citing military sources, claimed that government forces had advanced around Bab Al Mandab and retaken Mocha, while Houthi forces had retreated from parts of the coast.Saudi Arabia is providing significant military backing to the Yemeni government offensive. Major General Turki Al Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, said 100 fighter jets took part in operations on Monday and that the coalition was providing continuous air support to Yemeni forces. He said 324 “high-value” targets had been destroyed.The escalation also prompted an emergency meeting of the Makkah Alliance for Defence, bringing together Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye. The three countries agreed to move towards the implementation of collective-defence commitments, including the rapid deployment of agreed military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia, subject to existing arrangements and the national laws of the member states.The developments today mark a major escalation in Yemen, with the internationally recognised government seeking to reverse Houthi territorial gains, Saudi Arabia providing military backing and the Houthis threatening Saudi airspace.

. India and Uruguay will face each other today in a FIFA international friendly football match at the Yuva Bharati Krirangan in Salt Lake. India had earlier played out a 1-1 draw against Panama and suffered a 0-4 defeat to Brazil on Saturday. Learning from the mistakes of their previous match, the Indian team will be looking to put up a strong performance against two-time world champions Uruguay in their final friendly. India coach Khalid Jamil said there was a lack of coordination among the players in the last match. He said the players will remain alert from the very first minute against Uruguay.Uruguay coach Diego Forlán, meanwhile, said India have several skilled players capable of putting their opponents under pressure. He added that Uruguay are not taking the Indian team lightly.

The UAE’s General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) has announced that the transfer of passengers to Tel Aviv has been completed following the temporary suspension of flydubai flights to the destination.The GCAA said 37 flights were operated from Dubai International Airport to Ben Gurion Airport between October 2 and October 5, carrying 7,479 passengers. As an alternative to the suspended flydubai services, UAE authorities also granted permits to Israeli carriers to operate flights to Dubai, alongside Etihad Airways services. The aviation regulator said coordination is now complete for passengers whose flights were disrupted and who were left stranded, with those passengers now returned to their destinations.The Emirates News Agency (WAM), citing the UAE aviation regulator, reported that Etihad Airways continues to operate scheduled flights to Tel Aviv, providing additional travel options for passengers.

Similar conditions are likely to prevail over Sikkim, Chhattisgarh, East Madhya Pradesh, Madhya Maharashtra, Konkan, Goa, Lakshadweep, Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Northeastern states for the day.Meanwhile, the Met Department has said that the national Capital is expected to witness very light rain or drizzle today at a few places, accompanied with thunderstorm and lightning during afternoon or evening.
